newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank hikes capital demands on banks.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank hikes capital demands on banks.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) on Tuesday raised minimum capital requirements for local commercial banks nearly five-fold to adjust for inflation and seek to enforce international standards.

Under a capital adequacy regulation published in the State Gazette, banks will be required to maintain a minimum of 10 billion levs in equity capital by June 30, 1998, up from the current 2.2 billion levs for a full licence and 1.4 billion levs for a domestic one.
Investors applying for a new banking licence will be required to have at least 10 billion levs in capital by same deadline.
The current requirements were introduced by the BNB in 1996, but have quickly become inadequate through rampant inflation and the sharp fall in the lev.
Year-on-year consumer price inflation was 1,527 percent in June.

Local branches of foreign banks will not be required to have a minimum capital of 10 billion levs if they meet international capital adequacy standards and the foreign bank has the required capital in the country of registration.
An additional requirement for foreign banks is that they place with the BNB a permanent guarantee from the parent company to cover any liability of the branch.

Under the new BNB regulations, banks have to boost their capital-to-risk assets ratio to a minimum of eight percent by the end of this year, to 10 percent by end-1998 and to 12 percent by the end of 1999. -- Sofia Newsroom, 3592 911 88
